thread:
Jamie: Heads-up — I'm about to cut RC for the release candidate we talked about. Need quick confirmations: has the version bump landed on main and does the changelog entry exist? Also seeing a couple flaky failures in CI that we should triage before GA.

Priya: I pushed the bump and changelog earlier this morning, @Jamie. Tag and changelog are on `release/v2.5.x` — commit 9f3a2b7. :white_check_mark:

Mike: I can take the flaky tests. Which jobs are failing?

Jamie: macos-unit-tests and e2e-network are intermittently failing in the green sweep. ci-bot reported two flakes in the last 3 runs.

ci-bot: Build queued: #5678 (rc/2.5.3) — running
ci-bot: Job failures (recent): macos-unit-tests (4/12 runs), e2e-network (2/8 runs)

Anya: Noted. I'll rerun the macos job across the matrix and check logs. If it's the same stacktrace, we may pin the dependency or add a retry in the workflow.

SRE-Oncall: FYI, we've had a transient DNS hiccup in us-west-2 earlier; could have impacted e2e-network stability. I don't think it's a code regression but worth double-checking timestamps in the failing runs.

Mike: I'll start by running the failing tests locally in a macos-latest runner via the actions debug image. If I can reproduce, I'll open a tiny PR to add a targeted fixture or retry wrapper.

Jamie: Thanks. Also reminder: cutoff for RC->GA is in ~6 hours. If the flaky tests persist, we should consider canary gating (rollout to dedicated pool first) rather than holding the release. Can we have a short decision thread in the next 2 hours?

Priya: Changelog looks good to me. I added the migration note under "Breaking changes" and a short upgrade path.

Anya: Re-ran the macos-unit-tests on the last failing commit. Logs show a timing-based assertion in `session_manager_test.go`. Pasting snippet:
```
--- FAIL: TestSessionExpiry (0.00s)
    session_manager_test.go:142: expected 30s, got 29s
```
I can add a small tolerance and re-run the sweep.

Mike: If it's just timing noise, add a 200ms tolerance and mark the test as non-flaky with a follow-up ticket to improve determinism. I'll submit the PR now and trigger a green sweep.

release-bot: PR #3245 opened by Mike: "tests: relax session expiry timing to avoid CI flake" — checks: running

Jamie: Good. Once the PR is green, can we do one final full green sweep (all matrices) and then cut the RC tag? I'll do the tag and publish notes.

ci-bot: Build #5679 triggered by PR #3245 — macos-unit-tests: queued, e2e-network: queued

Priya: Quick ask — does the release notes include the known regressions list? We should call out the DNS transient and the e2e flake so customers are aware.

SRE-Oncall: I'll add a short note in the release doc about the DNS incident and link the incident page.

Jamie: Perfect. If all green within the sweep, I'll run `git tag -a v2.5.3-rc1 -m "v2.5.3 rc1"` and push. If not, we gate to canary and reconvene. :thumbsup:

Anya: PR #3245 is green on macos and looks promising. Starting the full sweep now.

Mike: Thanks everyone — ping me if any test surfaces a new failure.

release-bot: Sweep result: partial green (macos-ok, linux-ok, e2e-network still flaky). Recommendation: hold GA, proceed with canary on Dedicated pool and monitor telemetry for 2 hours.
